rationale: The pair is novel (no STRING record, no CellPhoneDB hit, 0 PubMed co-mentions) and compartment-compatible: both are brain-expressed plasma-membrane proteins. However, GRIN2D is an obligate subunit of heterotetrameric NMDA receptors (CellPhoneDB complex Glutamate_NMDA_1_2D_complex with GRIN1), and the fold used GRIN2D alone. The very large modeled interface (3225 A^2 buried, 639 contacts, interface pLDDT only 63.7, minimum separation 2.04 A) could sit on surfaces that GRIN1 or the second GRIN2 subunit occupies in the assembled receptor, so the dimer model cannot be accepted as it stands.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt annotates GRIN2D as a glycoprotein with 6 glycosylation sites (plus 4 disulfide bonds and 2 modified residues) and GPR6 as a glycoprotein and palmitoylated lipoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites and 1 lipidation site. The glycans on both proteins are extracellular and AF3 did not model them; if the 3225 A^2 interface involves the GRIN2D extracellular amino-terminal or ligand-binding domains, or the GPR6 N-terminus, glycans could sterically interfere. Whether any site lies on the interface is unknown without per-residue analysis. The PubMed PTM searches (6 hits for GRIN2D, 8 for GPR6) returned only expression and disease papers, none specifically about PTMs relevant to this interface.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for GRIN2D and GPR6 returned 0 hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING returned no association for GRIN2D and GPR6. CellPhoneDB returned no curated interaction, and GPR6 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table. PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers. The pair is not previously reported.
follow_up: Folding was not available in this run. Recommended next steps: (1) Re-fold GPR6 with GRIN1 plus GRIN2D (ideally the 2:2 GRIN1/GRIN2D tetramer, or at least a GRIN1-GRIN2D heterodimer) and check whether the GPR6 interface persists on an exposed surface of the assembled receptor or overlaps the GRIN1 contact surface. (2) Inspect interface topology for a physically impossible mix of cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, and for the 6 GRIN2D and 3 GPR6 N-glycosylation sites at the contact surface. (3) Note the supplied specificity statistics are borderline: GPR6 was confident at 1 of 3 receptors tested, with p_twoway=0.053. (4) If the interface survives, test by co-immunoprecipitation or BRET in striatal neurons or co-transfected cells, checking whether constitutive GPR6 Gs/cAMP signalling modulates GluN2D-containing NMDAR currents.

rationale: No database or literature records this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, PubMed co-occurrence 0), and the supplied breadth control is specific (EFNA3 confident against 1 of 9 receptors tested, p_twoway 0.0145), so it is novel and not an obviously promiscuous fold. However, both proteins are UniProt glycoproteins (EFNA3 P52797: 3 glycosylation sites plus 1 GPI lipidation; GPR21 Q99679: 2 glycosylation sites), and the only face of a 7-transmembrane receptor that a GPI-anchored extracellular ephrin can reach is its small extracellular surface, where GPCR glycosylation sites sit. I could not run a fold to check whether those sites lie on the modelled interface, so this is an unverified inference. The reported interface (buried surface 5310 Å2, 1124 contacts, minimum separation 1.88 Å, interface pLDDT 68.4, ipTM 0.64) also looks larger than that extracellular face could plausibly supply, which raises the possibility that the model packs ephrin against transmembrane or cytoplasmic regions it could not physically reach. Expression support is weak.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt annotates EFNA3 (P52797) with the keywords Glycoprotein, GPI-anchor and Lipoprotein, and counts 3 glycosylation sites, 1 lipidation site and 2 disulfide bonds. UniProt annotates GPR21 (Q99679) as a Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites. The PubMed PTM search returned 11 hits for EFNA3 and 1 for GPR21, but the titles concern miR-210/EFNA3 signalling and plasmalogen signalling, not glycosylation, so they are uninformative. The concern is plausibly relevant because both glycosylated regions are extracellular, which is the only place the interaction could occur, and the GPR21 extracellular face is small. Whether any glycosylation site actually lies on the modelled interface was not verified, because no per-residue or fold tool was available in this run.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for EFNA3 and GPR21 returned 0 hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING returned no association for the pair. CellPhoneDB returned no curated interaction, and GPR21 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table. PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers. UniProt describes EFNA3 as a ligand for Eph receptor tyrosine kinases and GPR21 as an orphan receptor. The pair is novel with respect to these sources.
follow_up: 1. Re-fold EFNA3 (mature ectodomain, without the signal peptide and GPI propeptide) with GPR21, and read the interface topology. If the interface touches GPR21 transmembrane-core or cytoplasmic residues, treat the prediction as an artifact. 2. If the interface is purely extracellular, check whether the GPR21 N-linked sites or the 3 EFNA3 glycosylation sites lie on it, and if so re-fold with the core glycans attached. 3. Inspect the 1.88 Å minimum separation for clashes. 4. Consider a competition fold with an Eph receptor ligand-binding domain (for example EPHA2 or EPHA4, which are EFNA3's canonical partners per UniProt, not CellPhoneDB complex members) to see whether the GPR21 contact uses the same ephrin loop. 5. Wet-lab test if the above pass: binding of EFNA3-Fc to cells expressing GPR21, with and without PNGase treatment.

rationale: IGF2 is a secreted hormone (HPA: "Secreted to blood", function "Hormone") and GPRC5C is a 7-transmembrane orphan GPCR that HPA places at the plasma membrane, so a ligand-receptor geometry is compartmentally plausible. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence all returned nothing for the pair, so it is novel. The structural support is borderline: ipTM is 0.49, just under the 0.5 convention, and interface pLDDT is 64.7, although interface PAE is 2.15 A and IGF2 was confident against only 1 of 17 receptors tested (p_twoway=0.020548). Treat this as a novel but unproven hypothesis, not a confident prediction.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: GPRC5C (UniProt Q9NQ84) carries the keywords Glycoprotein and Phosphoprotein, with 1 annotated glycosylation site and 6 modified residues. The glycosylation site's position relative to the modeled interface is unknown; if it lies on the extracellular N-terminal region, a glycan there could sterically affect an extracellular IGF2 contact that AF3 modeled from bare sequence. The PubMed PTM search for GPRC5C returned 2 papers, neither specifically about glycosylation (angiotensin II-induced smooth muscle contraction; branched-chain amino acid metabolism in leukemogenesis). The uniprot_annotation lookup for IGF2 returned the wrong entry (Q6U949, "Putative insulin-like growth factor 2 antisense gene protein") rather than IGF2 itself, so no usable UniProt PTM data were obtained for IGF2. The PubMed PTM search for IGF2 returned 250 papers, but the top titles are about IGF2 signalling, not about IGF2 modification. This is an unresolved caveat, not evidence of an artifact.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for IGF2 and GPRC5C returned 0 hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING returned no association for IGF2 and GPRC5C. CellPhoneDB returned no curated interaction, and GPRC5C is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table at all. PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers. No hit in any of the three sources supports genuine novelty.
follow_up: 1) Fold IGF2 (the true entry, P01344, mature peptide only, without the signal peptide and E-domain) with GPRC5C, and read the interface topology: the contacts must fall on GPRC5C's extracellular N-terminus, extracellular loops or transmembrane bundle, not its cytoplasmic tail. In the same fold, check whether the single GPRC5C N-glycosylation site lies on the interface; if it does, re-fold with the glycan attached. 2) Confirm that the chain-pair ipTM clears 0.5 with additional seeds, since the current 0.49 is below the convention. 3) Compare against IGF2 folded with its established receptors IGF1R, IGF2R and INSR as positive controls (these are listed as other_subunits for that benchmarking purpose only; no tool evidence indicates GPRC5C forms a complex with them). 4) Wet-lab: test IGF2 binding to GPRC5C-expressing cells by SPR or a cell-surface binding assay, with IGF1R/IGF2R blockade to exclude signal from the canonical receptors.

rationale: GNRH2 (UniProt O43555, progonadoliberin-2) is HPA-classed "Predicted secreted proteins", secreted to blood, function "hormone"; MRGPRX2 (Q96LB1) is a plasma-membrane GPCR whose documented function is to be a promiscuous mast-cell receptor for BASIC secretagogue peptides (substance P, cortistatin-14, PAMP-12, LL-37, beta-defensins, dynorphins, PMX-53), so a cationic decapeptide hormone binding it is mechanistically the right class of interaction rather than an implausible one. No prior evidence exists for this specific pair: STRING returned found=false, CellPhoneDB returned no match, and pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for GNRH2 + MRGPRX2. The secreted-ligand/membrane-receptor geometry means same-cell coexpression is not required, so the ipTM=0.65 / interface PAE 2.2 A model is a genuinely novel, testable ligand hypothesis.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: Neither protein carries a glycosylation or lipidation concern: GNRH2's ptm_topology_feature_counts show only 1 "Modified residue" and no Glycosylation; MRGPRX2 shows only 2 Disulfide bonds (AF3 handles cysteine proximity acceptably) and no Glycosylation. The real caveat is different and processing-related: GNRH2's UniProt keywords include "Amidation" and "Cleavage on pair of basic residues", i.e. the bioactive species is the C-terminally amidated decapeptide excised from the 86-residue precursor, whereas AF3 was given the bare unprocessed sequence. pubmed_ptm_glycosylation for GNRH2 returned 6 hits, all about GnRH receptor signalling in fish/pig rather than modification of the human peptide; the 41 MRGPRX2 hits are mast-cell degranulation papers unrelated to receptor PTMs.
known_interaction_evidence: string_known_interaction: found=false (no channel, no textmining). cellphonedb_known_interaction: found=false, no matches. pubmed_cooccurrence: count=0, no hits. All three are negative, which is fairly strong evidence of genuine novelty for this pair.
follow_up: I could not run fold_complex in this session (tool unavailable). Recommended fold: re-run AF3 with ONLY the mature amidated GnRH-II decapeptide (pGlu-His-Trp-Ser-His-Gly-Trp-Tyr-Pro-Gly-NH2), not the full precursor, against MRGPRX2, and read the structural_analysis to confirm the peptide sits inside the transmembrane bundle (the orthosteric site used by substance P and the other basic secretagogues) rather than draped on the extracellular loops. Bench test: MRGPRX2-transfected HEK293 or LAD2/human skin mast cell calcium-flux and beta-hexosaminidase release assays with synthetic GnRH-II, with a MRGPRX2-knockout or antagonist (e.g. QWF) control, and a counter-screen against GNRHR/GNRHR2 to show the response is MRGPRX2-specific.

rationale: GHRL (UniProt Q9UBU3) is a secreted hormone precursor whose documented binding mechanism is lipid-dependent: UniProt states "Octanoylated ghrelin-28 is the most commonly found ghrelin and octanoylation is essential for the activation of the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1 (GHSR)", with keyword "Lipoprotein" and 3 annotated Lipidation features — a modification AF3 does not represent in a bare-sequence fold, so the modeled GHRL surface is not the physiological, acylated ligand surface. MRGPRX4 (Q96LA9) is moreover not a peptide receptor at all but a G protein-coupled receptor for bile acids (deoxycholate, chenodeoxycholate, 3-sulfated bile acids), whose orthosteric pocket is built for a small sterol-like ligand, making a 3046 Å² peptide interface at ipTM 0.65 chemically off-mechanism. No prior evidence links the pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, PubMed co-occurrence 0), so the pair is novel, but novelty here most likely reflects an unmodeled-PTM/wrong-ligand-class artifact rather than a real ligand-receptor hypothesis.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: GHRL: UniProt keywords include "Lipoprotein" and "Amidation"; ptm_topology_feature_counts show Lipidation x3 and Modified residue x1. The Ser3 octanoylation is explicitly described as essential for receptor activation, i.e. the real binding mechanism is lipid-mediated and entirely absent from AF3's bare-sequence model. MRGPRX4: keyword "Glycoprotein" with 2 Glycosylation sites and 2 disulfide bonds; whether a glycan sits on the modeled interface could not be checked (fold_complex unavailable in this run). PubMed PTM searches were largely off-target (GHRL hits concern tau pathology, avian GH release, frailty biomarkers; MRGPRX4 hits concern phospho-drug pruritus and a phosphorylation switch for lipid GPCR activators).
cooccurrence_evidence: pubmed_cooccurrence(GHRL, MRGPRX4) = 0 hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: no association found for GHRL–MRGPRX4. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction (MRGPRX4 is not even in the CellPhoneDB gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers mentioning both genes. By the novelty criteria this pair is genuinely unreported.
follow_up: Re-run the AF3 multimer with the mature acylated ghrelin peptide (Ser3 n-octanoyl) rather than the bare prepropeptide, and with MRGPRX4's two N-glycans represented, to see whether the interface survives and whether the contacts fall inside the transmembrane bundle (the bile-acid orthosteric site) or merely on extracellular loops — I could not run this fold in the current session. Wet-lab test would be a Gq/calcium-mobilisation or IP3 assay in MRGPRX4-expressing cells with acyl- and des-acyl-ghrelin, plus a competition assay against deoxycholate 3-sulfate; a GHSR-expressing line is the positive control.

rationale: No database or literature records this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, PubMed 0 hits), and a secreted plasma protein meeting a cell-surface GPCR is topologically permissible. However, FGA does not circulate alone: CellPhoneDB lists it in the obligate fibrinogen complex with FGB and FGG, so a fold of the bare alpha chain exposes coiled-coil and disordered surface that is buried or differently arranged in the real molecule. The model is also marginal and not specific: ipTM is 0.53, interface pLDDT is 68.8, p_twoway is 0.051, and FGA scored as confident against 2 of the 3 receptors it was tested with.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt marks FGA (P02671) as a Glycoprotein and Phosphoprotein with 4 glycosylation sites, 16 modified residues and 8 disulfide bonds; it is also cleaved by thrombin and cross-linked through isopeptide bonds. UniProt marks GPR101 (Q96P66) as a Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites and 1 disulfide bond; the 2 sites were not mapped to a domain. The PubMed PTM searches (22 hits for FGA, 1 for GPR101) returned nothing specific to this interface. Glycans on either protein could sit on an extracellular contact surface, but whether any glycosylation site lies on the modeled interface was not determined, so this is a secondary caveat and not the basis for the verdict.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for FGA and GPR101 returned 0 hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING returned no association for FGA and GPR101. CellPhoneDB returned no curated interaction, and GPR101 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table. PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers. The pair is novel with respect to these sources. GPR101 is annotated by UniProt as an orphan receptor.
follow_up: No fold was run for this triage. Recommended: (1) re-fold GPR101 with FGA plus FGB plus FGG (one alpha/beta/gamma half-molecule) and see whether the GPR101 interface persists at chain-pair ipTM of at least 0.5 on a surface that is exposed in assembled fibrinogen. (2) Check that the interface residues on GPR101 are extracellular or transmembrane-boundary only, not cytoplasmic. (3) Check whether any of the 4 FGA or 2 GPR101 glycosylation sites lie on the interface. (4) Inspect the 1.85 Å minimum separation for clashes and check whether the 3470 Å2 interface is driven by FGA's disordered alpha-C region. (5) Counter-screen FGA against more unrelated GPCRs, since 2 of 3 receptors tested were already confident, which suggests non-specific docking.

rationale: The pair is unreported (STRING found nothing, CellPhoneDB found nothing, PubMed co-occurrence count 0) and biologically possible: both are membrane proteins, both HPA-annotated at the primary cilium, and FGFR1 is broadly expressed so it should be present in the pituitary lactotrophs where GPR50 is enriched. The structural support is contradictory, though: ipTM is 0.38, below the 0.5 convention for a predicted interaction, and p_twoway is 0.058, while interface PAE is 2.42 A and only 1 of 4 partner receptors tested passed the PAE gate. The side of the membrane the interface sits on could not be checked without a fold, and FGFR1 has 8 glycosylation sites, so neither a novel-interaction call nor an artifact call is supported.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt lists FGFR1 as a Glycoprotein with 8 glycosylation sites (on its extracellular immunoglobulin domains), plus the keywords Heparin-binding and Phosphoprotein and 7 modified residues. GPR50 has no glycosylation or lipidation features in UniProt (1 disulfide bond only). The PubMed PTM search returned 674 hits for FGFR1 and 4 for GPR50, but the titles shown were not specific to glycosylation at any interface. Whether a glycosylation site lies on the modeled interface is unknown, because the interface residues and their topology were not available. If the contact involves the FGFR1 ectodomain, glycan occlusion is a real concern; if it is transmembrane or cytoplasmic, it is not.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for FGFR1 and GPR50 returned 0 hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING returned no association for FGFR1 and GPR50. CellPhoneDB returned no curated interaction, and GPR50 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table. PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers. The pair is novel as far as these sources show. As precedent only, UniProt (Q13585) describes GPR50 activating another single-pass receptor kinase, TGFBR1, by interfering with FKBP1A binding; this is not evidence for FGFR1.
follow_up: Re-fold FGFR1 with GPR50 and read the interface topology to establish whether the contact is ectodomain, transmembrane or cytoplasmic, and whether any of the 8 FGFR1 glycosylation sites sit on it; this could not be run here. The very large interface (buried surface area 7088 A^2, 1306 contacts, interface pLDDT 64.7, minimum separation 2.16 A) across a 1439-token complex should be inspected in 3D for extended low-confidence packing rather than a discrete interface, and for any interface touching both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues at once (physically impossible; AF3 models no bilayer). Consider truncating the long GPR50 C-terminal tail and folding domain-level constructs to see whether ipTM rises above 0.5. CellPhoneDB lists FGFR1 in a Klotho_FGFR1 complex with KL, and FGFR1 normally signals as an FGF/heparan-sulfate-bound dimer, so a fold with a co-receptor or ligand is a reasonable secondary test. If the fold holds up, test by co-immunoprecipitation or BRET in a pituitary lactotroph-derived or hypothalamic cell line.

rationale: WNT3 (secreted) and the orphan GPCR GPR101 (cell membrane) are a compartment-plausible ligand/receptor pair with no prior record in STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed (0 co-mentions), so the pair is novel. However, UniProt annotates WNT3 (P56703) as a Lipoprotein and Glycoprotein (1 lipidation site, 2 glycosylation sites) and GPR101 (Q96P66) as a Glycoprotein (2 glycosylation sites), none of which AF3's bare-sequence model represents; Wnt receptor engagement is generally understood (background knowledge, not from the tools) to depend on the lipid modification. The fold itself is only marginal (ipTM 0.55, interface pLDDT 67.7, p_twoway 0.053), and I could not check whether any modification site actually sits on the modeled interface, so the artifact call is a caution, not a demonstrated result.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: WNT3 (UniProt P56703): keywords Lipoprotein and Glycoprotein; feature counts are 1 lipidation, 2 glycosylation and 11 disulfide bonds. The PubMed PTM search returned 52 hits, including PMID 38994173, "N-glycosylation of Wnt3 regulates the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma by affecting Wnt/β-catenin signal pathway". GPR101 (UniProt Q96P66): keyword Glycoprotein; 2 glycosylation sites and 1 disulfide bond; the PubMed PTM search returned 1 hit, which is not about GPR101 glycosylation. The WNT3 lipid and the glycans on both proteins are absent from the AF3 model and are plausibly relevant to an extracellular ligand/receptor interface, but whether any of these sites lies on the modeled interface could not be checked because no fold tool was available in this run.
cooccurrence_evidence: pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for WNT3 and GPR101.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: no association found for WNT3 and GPR101. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction, and GPR101 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is unreported. UniProt describes WNT3 as a ligand for frizzled-family seven-transmembrane receptors and GPR101 as an orphan receptor.
follow_up: 1) Not run here (fold tools unavailable): re-fold WNT3 with GPR101 and read the structural analysis for (a) whether the WNT3 lipidation site, the 2 WNT3 glycosylation sites or the 2 GPR101 glycosylation sites sit on the interface, and (b) whether the GPR101 contact residues are Extracellular/Transmembrane rather than Cytoplasmic. If an N-glycosylation site is on the interface, re-fold with the glycan attached. 2) FZD7 and LRP6 in other_subunits are not tool-derived (CellPhoneDB returned no complexes for either protein); they are suggested from general knowledge of canonical Wnt receptors as a comparison fold, to see whether WNT3 uses the same surface on GPR101 as it would on a Frizzled receptor. 3) The supplied breadth data show WNT3 was confident against only 1 of 5 receptors tested, which argues against a generically sticky ligand; a wet-lab test would be binding or signalling of lipidated WNT3 conditioned medium on GPR101-expressing cells.

rationale: CADM4 and GPR37 are both membrane proteins enriched in brain and in oligodendrocytes (HPA), and UniProt independently ties both to oligodendrocyte differentiation and CNS myelination, so a cis interaction on the same cell is biologically plausible. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed (0 papers) all return nothing for the pair, so it is novel. Confidence is low because the supplied ipTM of 0.47 is below the 0.5 convention for a predicted interaction (despite interface PAE 2.54 A and 1 of 8 partner receptors passing the gate), interface pLDDT is only 65.3, and both ectodomains carry 3 N-glycosylation sites each whose position relative to the interface could not be checked without a fold.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt: CADM4 (Q8NFZ8) is a glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites, 1 lipidation (palmitoylation) site and 3 disulfide bonds; its function text says the palmitoylated form is required for oligodendrocyte maturation and myelination via association with CADM2/3 and MAG. GPR37 (O15354) is a glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites and 1 disulfide bond. The PubMed PTM searches returned 3 hits for CADM4 and 10 for GPR37, but the titles shown do not concern glycosylation of either protein's interface (the GPR37 top hit is about glycosylation of its ligand prosaposin). Glycans on either ectodomain could occlude the modeled contact surface if the interface is extracellular; this could not be checked per residue because no fold was available in this run. This is a real but unresolved caveat, not a demonstrated artifact.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers mentioning CADM4 and GPR37 together.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction for the pair. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. No evidence anywhere that this pair is already reported.
follow_up: 1) Re-fold CADM4 + GPR37 and read the interface topology: confirm the contacts are extracellular/transmembrane on both chains and not a mix of cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, and check whether any of the 3 N-glycosylation sites on each protein lies on the interface; if one does, re-fold with the glycan attached. The very large buried area (3453 A2, 631 contacts) at interface pLDDT 65.3 and a minimum separation of 1.77 A suggests extensive transmembrane-helix packing or a loosely packed model, which should be inspected in 3D. 2) The ipTM of 0.47 is below 0.5, so treat the model as a hypothesis only. 3) Wet-lab test: co-immunoprecipitation or proximity ligation of CADM4 and GPR37 in oligodendrocyte cultures or co-transfected cells, ideally also with CADM4 palmitoylation-deficient mutant. 4) CellPhoneDB lists no complexes for either protein; the suggested other subunits (CADM2, CADM3, MAG) come only from the UniProt function text for CADM4, and a CORUM check is still needed.

rationale: I'm downgrading from CONFIRMED_NOVEL. The two proteins are not secreted, so any direct contact would require them to sit in the same membrane. HPA shows no shared protein-level tissue. My earlier co-expression argument rested only on both being enhanced in bone marrow MSCs (RNA level, nCPM 671.6 and 56.6), which doesn't establish protein-level co-localization. The fold check also flags a topology violation, which fits my earlier worry that the 6079 A^2 interface spans both sides of the membrane. That is not a physically possible contact between two single membrane-embedded receptors, so the AF3 confidence (ipTM 0.66, interface pLDDT 60.3) is not credible support. Absence of any STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed record (0 papers) means nothing offsets these concerns. The glycosylation caveat (ROR2 has 3 sites, MRGPRF has 1) is unresolved but no longer decides the verdict. Confidence stays low because the MSC RNA overlap leaves a small chance of real co-localization.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: ROR2 has 3 annotated glycosylation sites and MRGPRF has 1. Neither function text describes glycan-mediated binding, and the interface location is unknown. This is an unresolved caveat, not the basis for the verdict.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for ROR2 and MRGPRF returned 0 hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence (0 papers) all show no prior record of the pair. known_interaction_strength=none.
follow_up: Only revisit if protein-level co-expression is shown in the same cell type, for example through MSC proteomics. If so, re-fold the pair using only the extracellular domains, so the topology is physically consistent.

rationale: The pair is compartmentally plausible and unreported: galectin-3 is secreted (HPA "Secreted to blood") and GPR39 is a plasma-membrane GPCR, with no STRING or CellPhoneDB record and only one incidental PubMed co-mention. However, UniProt describes LGALS3 (P17931) as a "Galactose-specific lectin" and GPR39 (O43194) as a glycoprotein with 3 annotated glycosylation sites, so any real galectin-3 binding to GPR39 would be expected to go through GPR39's N-glycans, which the bare-sequence AF3 model does not contain. The AF3 protein-protein interface (ipTM 0.53, interface pLDDT 66.8, interface PAE 2.59 A, confident for 1 of 5 partner receptors tested) is borderline in ipTM and cannot represent that mechanism, so the modeled contact is more likely an artifact than a novel protein-protein interface.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt P17931 (LGALS3) function text begins "Galactose-specific lectin which binds IgE" and carries the keyword "Lectin"; its own feature counts show 4 modified residues and 1 disulfide bond and no glycosylation. UniProt O43194 (GPR39) carries the keyword "Glycoprotein" with 3 annotated Glycosylation features, plus 2 disulfide bonds and 1 modified residue. Galectin-3 binding to cell-surface receptors is canonically mediated by its carbohydrate-recognition domain binding beta-galactoside-containing glycans on the receptor, which AF3 does not model from bare sequence. The PubMed PTM searches returned 39 hits for LGALS3 and 25 for GPR39, but the titles shown are general disease/signalling papers and do not specifically address glycosylation of either protein, so the UniProt annotations are the basis for this caveat. Whether the 3 GPR39 glycosylation sites fall on the modeled interface is not known.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence count is 1: PMID 40616194, "DNA methylation and hydroxymethylation combined with transcriptional profiling identify key regulators of hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia" (Clin Epigenetics, 2025). This looks like an unrelated co-mention in an epigenomic/transcriptomic screen, not evidence of binding.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING returned no association for LGALS3-GPR39 (found: false). CellPhoneDB returned no curated interaction (found: false, no matches). PubMed co-occurrence returned 1 hit (PMID 40616194, a DNA methylation/hydroxymethylation and transcriptional profiling study of hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia), which appears to co-mention both genes in an omics gene list and is not a report of a direct interaction. The pair is therefore not already known.
follow_up: Folding was not available in this run. Recommended: (1) re-fold LGALS3 with GPR39 and read the interface topology to establish whether the modeled contact is on GPR39's extracellular face, its cytoplasmic face, or implausibly both, and whether any of the 3 UniProt N-glycosylation sites of GPR39 sit on the interface; (2) if a glycosylation site is on the interface, re-fold with the core N-glycan covalently attached at the true UniProt site and see whether the interface survives; (3) wet-lab test of glycan dependence, for example galectin-3 binding to GPR39-expressing cells with and without lactose competition or PNGase F treatment, and with a carbohydrate-recognition-domain mutant of galectin-3. CellPhoneDB lists no complexes for either protein; the other_subunits entries are the heteroreceptor partners named in the GPR39 UniProt function text (HTR1A and GALR1), given only as context and not as evidence of an obligate missing subunit. Note that the supplied breadth data show LGALS3 was confident against 1 of 5 receptors tested, so the fold is not broadly promiscuous, but galectin-3 has 167 known interactions in HPA and is a generally sticky glycan-binding hub.

rationale: The flagged contradiction holds up, so I'm changing the verdict from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE. Neither protein is secreted, so any direct contact would need both to be in the same place. HPA shows zero shared protein-level tissue and no shared enriched cell type. The fold check also reports a topology violation. The AF3 signal is borderline (ipTM 0.51, interface pLDDT 65.4), and the 3488 A^2 interface is unusually large for a weak prediction. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all return nothing for the pair, so nothing offsets these problems. GFRA3 is a GPI-anchored protein and GPR37L1 is a GPCR, so both are membrane proteins.
